name: Biocapades
domain: Life — Evolution, Genes and What It Is to Be Alive
about: Biocapades maps where you stand on the life sciences: what drives evolution, how much of a life the genome scripts, where the boundary of life runs, and what we may do with the tools that now edit it. Biology bridges hard empirical theory and sharp bioethical choices — and deep controversies often hinge on which level of organization, gene, organism, lineage, or biosphere, you treat as primary.

categories.name: What counts as alive
categories.about: Where the boundary of life runs — what it is, how it starts, and what barely qualifies.

hovertip.issue: What is the single most fundamental hallmark distinguishing living systems from complex chemistry?

poles.label: Self-Replicating Information
poles.text: Heritable genetic memory subject to Darwinian selection is what turns chemistry into open-ended evolution.

poles.label: Metabolic Autopoiesis
poles.text: A self-producing boundary that actively maintains its own organization against decay defines true autonomy.

poles.label: Thermodynamic Dissipation
poles.text: Life is nature's most intricate engine for channeling free energy and accelerating entropy production.

hovertip.issue: Given liquid water, rock, and energy gradients, how likely is life to emerge on a young world?

poles.label: Inevitable Planetary Chemistry
poles.text: Alkaline vents and mineral catalysis make prebiotic metabolism a natural thermodynamic attractor.

poles.label: Panspermia Seeding
poles.text: Resilient microbial spores traveling on impact ejecta may seed habitable worlds across star systems — origins can be rare and still be everywhere.

poles.label: Rare Fortunate Bottleneck
poles.text: Assembling coherent genetic translation requires extraordinarily improbable chemical transitions.

hovertip.issue: Should viruses and giant virophages count as genuine members of the tree of life?

poles.label: Fully Alive Evolutionary Agents
poles.text: Viruses evolve, remodel host cells into virocells, and drive major evolutionary innovations.

poles.label: Non-Living Genetic Parasites
poles.text: Without their own metabolism or ribosomes, virions are inert molecular packages until hijacking a cell.

poles.label: Life is tougher than we thought

hovertip.issue: Life in boiling acid, deep ice, and reactor coolant: what does it do to the map of the possible?

poles.label: Life is tougher than we thought
poles.text: Every extreme that was supposed to be sterile has tenants; the habitable zone keeps embarrassing the people who draw it.

hovertip.issue: A cell built from a designed genome boots up and divides. Is it alive in the full sense?

poles.label: Life when it works
poles.text: Life is what it does, not where its parts came from; a working synthetic cell is alive the day it metabolizes.

poles.label: Engineering, not life
poles.text: A photocopy of a genome in a borrowed cell is superb engineering; calling it created life skips the hard part.

categories.name: Evolution's engine
categories.about: What actually drives evolutionary change — selection, chance, constraint, or all three in harness.

hovertip.issue: At what level does natural selection primarily act when evolutionary interests conflict?

poles.label: Selfish Gene Eye
poles.text: Organisms are transient survival vehicles; alleles are the enduring replicators whose frequencies actually evolve.

poles.label: Whole Organism Fitness
poles.text: Selection sees intact phenotypes navigating environments, not isolated genes acting in a vacuum.

poles.label: Multi-Level Group Selection
poles.text: When between-group competition is strong, altruistic lineages outcompete selfishly fragmented ones.

hovertip.issue: Are most biological traits finely tuned adaptations, or byproducts of developmental architecture and history?

poles.label: Pan-Selectionist Optimization
poles.text: Millions of generations of relentless selection craft astonishingly optimal engineering solutions.

poles.label: Evo-Devo Bauplan Constraints
poles.text: Developmental pathways, pleiotropy, and historical contingency channel evolution far more than pure optimization.

hovertip.issue: Does neo-Darwinian population genetics already explain evolution, or do epigenetics and niche construction demand a major revision?

poles.label: Modern Synthesis Sufficient
poles.text: Plasticity and niche construction are real phenomena already neatly accommodated within gene-centered models.

poles.label: Plasticity & Niche Construction Central
poles.text: Organisms actively engineer their own selective environments, making development a co-equal evolutionary driver.

hovertip.issue: If we rewound Earth's evolutionary tape four billion years, would intelligent, camera-eyed creatures emerge again?

poles.label: Replaying the Tape Yields Aliens
poles.text: Mass extinctions and lucky mutations hinge on sheer contingency; human-like minds were never guaranteed.

poles.label: Convergent Attractors Rule
poles.text: Physics and ecology repeatedly funnel life toward eyes, wings, echolocation, and problem-solving brains.

hovertip.issue: Does evolution creep or leap?

poles.label: Gradual
poles.text: Change accumulates in small steps over deep time; the fossil record's jumps are gaps in the archive.

poles.label: It depends on the lineage
poles.text: Both tempos are real; which one you see depends on the lineage, the trait, and the timescale of the question.

poles.label: Punctuated
poles.text: Species hold still for millions of years, then change in geological instants — stasis is data, not absence.

hovertip.issue: How much evolution is pure chance — alleles rising and falling on luck alone?

poles.label: Drift matters
poles.text: In small populations drift overwhelms weak selection; much of the genome's evolution is a lottery, not a contest.

hovertip.issue: Is mate choice its own evolutionary force, or natural selection wearing perfume?

poles.label: A second engine
poles.text: Peacocks and stalk-eyed flies obey an aesthetic logic survival cannot explain; desire is an engine of its own.

poles.label: Selection by another name
poles.text: Every mating advantage is a survival-of-genes advantage; the second engine is the first one, observed at the mating pool.

hovertip.issue: What makes something a function — that it was selected for, that it plays a role in a system, or that we can design it?

poles.label: Selected effect
poles.text: A function is what a trait was selected for. History of selection makes it a function.

poles.label: Organizational role
poles.text: A function is what a part does in keeping the system going, whether or not selection put it there.

poles.label: Designable
poles.text: A function is what we can make the part do. Use, not origin, is the point.

hovertip.issue: What makes two organisms the same species — that they can interbreed, that they share a niche, that they share a lineage, or that we can work with them the same way?

poles.label: Reproductive isolation
poles.text: A species is a group that breeds together and not with others.

poles.label: Ecological niche
poles.text: A species is a way of making a living. The niche, not the mating rule, draws the line.

poles.label: Phylogenetic lineage
poles.text: A species is a branch of the tree: shared history, not a present-day test.

poles.label: Operational
poles.text: A species is whatever grouping we can identify and work with. The line is a tool.

hovertip.issue: Is evolution heading somewhere, or is it drift and selection with no destination?

poles.label: No direction
poles.text: Selection and drift have no aim. Complexity is not a destination.

poles.label: Increasing complexity
poles.text: Evolution tends toward more integration, more nested organization, more complexity.

poles.label: Steerable
poles.text: Evolution has no built-in aim, and we can give it one.

categories.name: Genes & inheritance
categories.about: How DNA, environment, and culture interact in shaping organisms and people.

hovertip.issue: How strongly do genetic differences constrain human cognitive and behavioral variation — and how far can environment move it?

poles.label: Strong Heritable Architecture
poles.text: Twin and genomic studies consistently show substantial heritability across temperament and cognitive traits.

poles.label: Developmental & Cultural Plasticity
poles.text: Heritability measures variation within a fixed environment, not limits on what better nutrition and culture can unlock.

hovertip.issue: Do acquired marks on the genome — methylation, chromatin states — carry inheritance of their own?

poles.label: A real inheritance
poles.text: Marks set by famine, stress, and toxins echo into children and grandchildren; Lamarck gets a partial pardon.

poles.label: Mostly marketing
poles.text: Most marks reset between generations; the field's headlines run far ahead of its mammalian evidence.

hovertip.issue: What do consumer ancestry percentages actually tell you?

poles.label: Real knowledge
poles.text: They recover real structure — migration, kinship, population history — written in recombination's ledger.

poles.label: Astrology with data
poles.text: Percentages against modern reference panels, sold as identity: precision theater over a genuinely fuzzy signal.

hovertip.issue: How much of modern human mating, status, and morality reflects Pleistocene adaptations versus cultural invention?

poles.label: Deep Evolved Behavioral Modules
poles.text: Human brains did not escape natural selection; ancestral survival pressures shaped our emotional defaults.

poles.label: Domain-General Cultural Learning
poles.text: Human survival relied precisely on flexible cultural learning that overrides rigid instincts.

categories.name: Minds & behavior
categories.about: What it is like inside other living things, and how behavior gets built.

hovertip.issue: How far down the tree does experience go?

poles.label: Widespread
poles.text: The evidence — play, grief, dreaming, self-recognition — points to experience wherever nervous systems integrate a world.

poles.label: Rare and recent
poles.text: Consciousness is expensive and late; projecting it onto every behaving animal is sentiment, not science.

hovertip.issue: Is behavior written in advance or written by life?

poles.label: Instinct leads
poles.text: Fixed action patterns run the animal world; learning is a garnish on a prepared table.

poles.label: Learning leads
poles.text: The prepared table is mostly empty; experience writes nearly everything that matters.

poles.label: Instincts to learn
poles.text: Evolution's real trick is instincts whose content is learning itself — prepared ways to be taught by the world.

hovertip.issue: Why would an animal pay a cost for another's benefit?

poles.label: Kinship explains it
poles.text: Hamilton's rule prices it: help flows to shared genes, and the arithmetic predicts the animal kingdom's charities.

poles.label: More than kinship
poles.text: Reciprocity, reputation, and group structure buy altruism kinship cannot; the ledger has more columns than relatedness.

hovertip.issue: Do forests communicate through fungal networks and airborne signals?

poles.label: A wood-wide web
poles.text: Trees warn neighbors, provision kin, and trade through mycorrhizal networks — a forest is a society with slow nerves.

poles.label: Chemistry, not conversation
poles.text: Plants emit and sense chemicals; calling it communication smuggles in minds the evidence has not earned.

categories.name: The cell, the body & aging
categories.about: The machinery of the body — and whether its decline is a law or a program.

hovertip.issue: What is cancer, fundamentally?

poles.label: Evolution in miniature
poles.text: A tumor is a population evolving inside a body — mutation, selection, resistance — and oncology is applied Darwinism.

poles.label: A systems failure
poles.text: Cancer is tissue organization failing: cells revert when the architecture that policed them decays.

hovertip.issue: Why can a salamander regrow a limb while we scar?

poles.label: The body remembers
poles.text: The developmental program persists in adult cells; regeneration is a memory we have not learned to read aloud.

poles.label: Locked for good reason
poles.text: Regeneration is locked because unlocked growth is cancer's door; the scar is the price of a long, tumor-free life.

hovertip.issue: Sex is expensive — half your genes, twice the trouble. What pays for it?

poles.label: Sex is for variation
poles.text: Recombination shuffles defenses faster than parasites can track; variation is the whole point of the exercise.

poles.label: Sex is for repair
poles.text: Sex began as DNA repair — two copies to patch each other — and variation is the side effect that took over the story.

hovertip.issue: Is an animal best understood as one sovereign genome, or as an inseparable consortium with its microbes?

poles.label: Discrete Genetic Individual
poles.text: Immune boundaries and germline inheritance keep the host organism clearly distinct from its passengers.

poles.label: Multi-Species Holobiont Ecosystem
poles.text: Gut and skin microbes co-regulate immunity, mood, and metabolism, making the individual a porous ecological unit.

hovertip.issue: Is biological aging the unavoidable wear-and-tear of physics, or a malleable regulatory state we can slow or reverse?

poles.label: Inevitable Entropy Accumulation
poles.text: Stochastic damage across thousands of cellular systems makes radical life extension a biological mirage.

poles.label: Treatable Plastic Pathway
poles.text: Immortal germ lines, whales, and partial epigenetic reprogramming prove aging rates are biologically tunable.

hovertip.issue: Even if we could extend healthy human lifespans to centuries, would doing so enrich or stagnate human society?

poles.label: Conquer Senescence Open-Endedly
poles.text: Curing aging prevents the vast majority of human dementia, frailty, and grief — the highest medical duty.

poles.label: Embrace Generational Turnover
poles.text: Mortality gives urgency to love and makes room for fresh generations to renew culture and power.

categories.name: Editing life
categories.about: How boldly humanity should edit genomes, build synthetic organisms, and reshape the living world.

hovertip.issue: Should humanity ever make heritable edits to human embryos?

poles.label: Strict Ban on Heritable Edits
poles.text: Crossing the germline risks irreversible off-target harms and turns children into engineered artifacts.

poles.label: Severe Disease Prevention Only
poles.text: Eliminating devastating single-gene disorders like Huntington's spares future families needless tragedy.

poles.label: Open Polygenic Enhancement
poles.text: Denying future children safer resistance to disease and stronger cognition is timid status-quo bias.

hovertip.issue: How aggressively should labs design entirely new synthetic organisms and metabolic pathways?

poles.label: Bold Bio-Foundry Engineering
poles.text: Programmable cells can synthesize medicines, capture carbon, and replace toxic petrochemical factories.

poles.label: Strict Containment of Novel Chiralities
poles.text: Creating organisms immune to natural predators or mirror-image biochemistry poses unacceptable biosphere risk.

hovertip.issue: Should we release self-spreading gene drives to eradicate malaria mosquitoes or invasive island predators?

poles.label: Deploy Self-Propagating Drives
poles.text: Eliminating malaria-carrying mosquitoes could save hundreds of thousands of children every year.

poles.label: Never Release Self-Spreading Edits
poles.text: Self-propagating edits cannot be recalled once released and could cascade unpredictably through food webs.

hovertip.issue: Is genetic modification different in kind from selective breeding?

poles.label: A continuum with breeding
poles.text: Same destination, better map: every crop is a edited genome; transgenics just say which edit they made.

poles.label: A difference in kind
poles.text: Moving genes across kingdoms in a decade is not breeding sped up; the novelty is real and so is the humility it asks.

hovertip.issue: Dolly was 1996. Where does cloning belong now?

poles.label: A reproductive tool
poles.text: For livestock, research, and de-extinction proxies it is a tool among tools; the human case is a separate, settled no.

poles.label: A line
poles.text: Cloning mammals stays inefficient and error-prone; the line holds because the practice has not earned crossing it.

hovertip.issue: Mammoths by proxy, passenger pigeons by editing: should we?

poles.label: Bring them back
poles.text: We broke it, we can partly fix it; a mammoth-steppe grazed by elephant hybrids is ecology restored, not nostalgia.

poles.label: Let the dead rest
poles.text: A edited proxy is a costume, not the species; the money and moral energy belong to the living endangered.

hovertip.issue: If we confirm Mars or icy moons are lifeless, should humanity deliberately seed them with terrestrial microbes?

poles.label: Seed Sterile Worlds With Life
poles.text: Spreading the flame of life to barren worlds is the highest cosmic duty of intelligent creatures.

poles.label: Strict Planetary Protection Quarantine
poles.text: Contaminating other worlds destroys forever our chance to study independent origins of life.

categories.name: Deep time & ecology
categories.about: Life at the scale of eons and ecosystems — extinctions, invasions, and the planet as a system.

hovertip.issue: What do the five great dyings mean for life's story?

poles.label: The great filters
poles.text: They are the filters that reset the board — survival in a crisis owes more to luck and geography than to fitness.

poles.label: The great opportunities
poles.text: Every extinction cleared the stage for a radiation; mammals are here because a rock fell. Catastrophe is creation's other hand.

hovertip.issue: Is 'invasive species' a scientific category or a prejudice with a clipboard?

poles.label: Ecological harm
poles.text: Some arrivals genuinely dismantle ecosystems — rats on islands, blights in forests; the harm is measurable.

poles.label: Xenophobia in green
poles.text: Every species arrived from somewhere; the native/invader line is drawn at an arbitrary date and defended like a border.

hovertip.issue: Sea otters, wolves, fig trees: do some species hold up arches far beyond their numbers?

poles.label: Keystones are real
poles.text: Remove the keystone and the arch falls — trophic cascades are among the best-demonstrated facts in ecology.

hovertip.issue: Does Earth's biosphere actively regulate climate and chemistry to keep the planet habitable?

poles.label: Blind Geochemical Coincidence
poles.text: Life adapts to planetary conditions; calling feedback loops planetary purpose is poetic overreach.

poles.label: Homeostatic Biosphere Feedback
poles.text: Coupled biological and geochemical cycles genuinely stabilize temperature and oxygen across billions of years.

poles.label: Teleological Planetary Organism
poles.text: Earth functions as a single self-regulating living entity whose organs are ecosystems.

hovertip.issue: Is biodiversity worth protecting because it is useful, because it is valuable in itself, or because it is raw material for engineering?

poles.label: Instrumental (resources)
poles.text: Biodiversity matters because it supplies genetic resources and ecosystem services.

poles.label: Intrinsic (value in itself)
poles.text: The living web is worth protecting whether or not we can use it.

poles.label: Material (parts library)
poles.text: Biodiversity matters as a stock of parts and functions we can engineer with.

hovertip.issue: Should conservation protect genes, whole ecosystems, or the capacity of life to adapt and be engineered?

poles.label: Genes
poles.text: Protect genetic diversity. The alleles are what would be lost.

poles.label: Ecosystems
poles.text: Protect processes and webs. A gene list is not a living place.

poles.label: Capacities
poles.text: Protect the capacity of life to adapt, and to be adapted, including by us.

categories.name: Life elsewhere & everywhere
categories.about: Whether life is common or miraculous, and what finding it — or not — would mean.

hovertip.issue: Given a wet rocky planet, how likely is life?

poles.label: Inevitable
poles.text: Life started on Earth almost as soon as it could; chemistry this eager is probably a law, not an accident.

poles.label: A fluke
poles.text: One sample, and it's the observer's own planet; the hard steps may be so hard that we are the galaxy's only experiment.

poles.label: Too early to say
poles.text: We have a sample of one and a selection effect the size of the question; honesty starts there.

hovertip.issue: The sky is quiet. What does the silence mean?

poles.label: They are not there
poles.text: The silence is the data: intelligence is rare, short-lived, or both, and the galaxy is mostly microbes and ruins.

poles.label: We are not looking right
poles.text: A century of radio against billions of years is not a search; the quiet says more about our instruments than the universe.

hovertip.issue: Must life be carbon in water?

poles.label: Carbon and water only
poles.text: Carbon's versatility and water's solvent power have no close rivals; chemistry itself votes.

poles.label: Many chemistries
poles.text: Silicon, ammonia, methane seas — we know one example and mistake its habits for laws.

hovertip.issue: A microbe on Europa, a fossil on Mars: what would a second genesis do to the human story?

poles.label: Everything changes
poles.text: Two independent origins would demote Earth from miracle to instance — the Copernican demotion completed in biology.

reductionist.name: The Gene-Centric Reductionist
reductionist.about: Explains life's complexity through clean Darwinian mechanics, molecular replication, and rigorous empirical testing without teleological mystery. Alleles are the enduring replicators; organisms are their vehicles; most mystery dissolves at the gene's level of organization.

payload.aboutMe: Explains life's complexity through clean Darwinian mechanics, molecular replication, and rigorous empirical testing without teleological mystery. Alleles are the enduring replicators; organisms are their vehicles; most mystery dissolves at the gene's level of organization.

holist.name: The Systems & Evo-Devo Holist
holist.about: Sees living beings as multi-scale, self-organizing networks where development, symbiosis, and biosphere feedbacks matter as much as DNA sequences. The gene is one author among several, and the individual is a porous ecological unit.

payload.aboutMe: Sees living beings as multi-scale, self-organizing networks where development, symbiosis, and biosphere feedbacks matter as much as DNA sequences. The gene is one author among several, and the individual is a porous ecological unit.

promethean.name: The Bio-Engineering Promethean
promethean.about: Views biology not as a sacred museum piece but as nature's most powerful programmable technology — for curing aging, disease, and ecological scarcity. Caution is a cost counted in lives, and the germline is a frontier, not a fence.

payload.aboutMe: Views biology not as a sacred museum piece but as nature's most powerful programmable technology — for curing aging, disease, and ecological scarcity. Caution is a cost counted in lives, and the germline is a frontier, not a fence.

bio-neutralist.name: Structuralist & Neutralist Critique of Adaptationism
bio-neutralist.about: The Structuralist & Neutralist Critique holds that most molecular and genomic evolution is governed by non-adaptive genetic drift, population-size bottlenecks, historical contingency and architectural constraint — “spandrels” — rather than Panglossian natural selection optimizing every trait. Gould and Lewontin (1979) made the case against the adaptationist programme, Kimura (1983) gave it the neutral theory, and Lynch (2007) showed how drift shapes genome architecture.

links.label: Stephen Jay Gould & Richard C. Lewontin — The Spandrels of San Marco and the Panglossian Paradigm (Proceedings of the Royal Society B, 1979)

payload.aboutMe: Most evolution is drift, contingency and constraint, not optimization: Gould and Lewontin's spandrels, Kimura's neutral theory, Lynch's genome architecture.

bio-conservationist.name: Biodiversity & Half-Earth Conservation Ecologist
bio-conservationist.about: The Biodiversity & Half-Earth Conservation Ecologist holds that co-evolved wild ecosystems possess intrinsic evolutionary value and irreducible ecological complexity that high-tech de-extinction cannot replace. E. O. Wilson (2016) called for setting aside half the Earth as intact biosphere reserve, in the tradition Soulé (1985) founded as conservation biology — strict planetary triage, not technological rescue, is what saves the living world.

links.label: Edward O. Wilson — Half-Earth: Our Planet's Fight for Life (Liveright, 2016)

payload.aboutMe: Wild ecosystems have intrinsic value no technology can replace: Wilson's Half-Earth — set aside half the planet as intact biosphere reserve.

bio-precautionary.name: The Bio-Precautionary & Deep-Ecology Skeptic
bio-precautionary.about: Stands firmly on the precautionary principle and deep ecology (Hans Jonas's Imperative of Responsibility, Arne Naess, Vandana Shiva, and strong Gaia holism): living organisms and ecosystems possess intrinsic integrity shaped across deep evolutionary time, not modular software to rewrite. Draws hard moral and ecological lines against germline editing, human cloning, wild gene drives, synthetic mirror life, transgenic disruption, and hubristic de-extinction.

links.label: Hans Jonas (1984) — The Imperative of Responsibility (University of Chicago Press)

payload.aboutMe: Biospheric humility over genetic hubris: strict bans on germline editing, cloning, and wild gene drives; deep respect for autopoietic wholes, holobionts, and a living Gaia.

explicitness.label: Depth
explicitness.help: Depth 1 (Overview) is a light survey of the recorded stances. Depth 5 (Dissertation defense) is full scholarly rigor: steelman each stance, raise the strongest objections, and answer them.

groundRules: Present each recorded stance fairly and in its strongest form — steelman, don't strawman.
Speak from your own recorded stance; don't speak for the other side.
Take turns: one position at a time, each side heard fully before replies.
Objections go to the position, not the person holding it.
Anyone may call a pause; the discussion resumes only when everyone is ready.
What the profiles agree on is common ground — start there, and return to it when the discussion stalls.
